name: encoding-utf8valid
algorithm: UTF-8 decode of valid text to an owned copy: a mixed-script line (ASCII, Latin-1, Cyrillic, CJK, one astral scalar) repeated n times, rounds times, each language's standard decoder; the checksum adds per round the output length and one output byte at a moving index (README.md).

skip.c: no UTF-8 decoder or validator in C's standard library
skip.mk-wrap: the checksum already uses the wrapping operators; the task has no other arithmetic to wrap

no_counts: B24 does not apply: an idiomatic row compares libraries; the decoder is tested by the lane's Go tests (TestStdEncoding_WptCases, TestStdEncoding_DecodeAdversarial, TestStdEncoding_LongInputs)
notes: Every column allocates its output afresh each round and frees it (std-encoding fix round, 2026-11-12: before it Mk reset one arena and Zig reused one buffer, so their output landed on warm pages while Rust and Go allocated). Mk: encoding.Utf8.Decode into a new Arena each round, freed at its end (one simd.ValidUtf8 pass, then a copy into an exact allocation). Rust: String::from_utf8_lossy(..).into_owned(), an owned String each round. Zig: std.unicode.utf8ValidateSlice and a copy into a buffer allocated and freed each round, fmtUtf8 only on a failed check. Go: bytes.ToValidUTF8, a new slice each round.

Every column returns an owned copy of the text, as Mk's Decode does; Rust's from_utf8_lossy alone and Go's strings.ToValidUTF8 return their valid input without copying, so the row asks each for the copy.
Checksums: Go's at both sizes on the owner's machine (std-encoding session 3, 2026-11-12); tools/bench verify checks the other columns.
Not published: no number here is a measurement.
